newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND SAYS NO QUICK FREE TRACT PACT WITH RUSSIA.
newsitem.headline: POLAND SAYS NO QUICK FREE TRACT PACT WITH RUSSIA.

text.p: Poland wants to liberalise trade with Russia but cannot sign a free trade agreement with Moscow soon because it is not a member of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Tuesday.
"We cannot rule it out (signing free trade agreement with Russia), but it would have to be subject to negotiations that would not be easy and short," said Cimoszwicz, who last week visited Russia.
"We have our standards of signing such agreements and these include a WTO membership," he told a news conference.
He said that under a joint declaration on trade libaralisation he had signed in Russia, the two countries' experts would work until March next year to lay grounds for further liberalisation talks.
Cimoszewicz said any trade relaxation with Russia would be consulted with the European Union, which Poland wants to join in the begining of the next century.

He also said Russian officials did not oppose Poland's plans to open branches of its banks in Russia despite small prospect for reciprocation, considering the Polish central bank's tight banking licence policy.
Cimoszewicz said Russian Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin had proposed that the two countries cooperate in military equipment production but that Poland had to think this over.
Trade between Poland and Russia collapsed in 1990 after the fall of communism but began to grow in the last few years. It is forecast to rise by about $1 billion in 1996 to $4 billion.

Trying to rebuild trade with the countries of the defunct Soviet-led Comecon bloc, Poland entered the Central Europe Free Trade Agreement, which also groups the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia and Slovenia.
